query_text: Make a mobile photo editing tool that feels like it belongs in a serious photographer's kit — the whole vibe should be rich and cinematic, centered around HDR and shadow recovery, where you can really bring back all that moody detail hiding in the dark parts of a shot and give highlights a natural glow rather than a blown-out look, with a beautifully designed editing screen that shows a before/after split so you can feel the transformation as you drag the sliders.

Create a mobile app for making job vacancy posting flyers that feels like it carries real professional weight — the kind of tool you'd actually trust to represent your company, with a set of clean, confident templates that let you plug in the role title, requirements, and contact info and instantly get something that looks intentional and put-together, not like a rushed printout, and a simple way to export or share it straight from your phone.

Make a presentation slide template gallery app for mobile that has a real curatorial identity to it — the kind of place where every template feels like it was chosen with taste, organized by vibe or purpose like "clean pitch" or "bold keynote", so when you're on your phone browsing for the right starting point you're not drowning in generic options but actually discovering something that matches the energy of your talk, and you can preview it full-screen before saving.

Create a mobile card-maker tool specifically for product launch announcements that has a strong sense of style — something that feels like it was designed for brands that care about first impressions, with a handful of bold, editorial-feeling templates you can customize with your product name, a punchy tagline, launch date, and a hero image, giving you a finished card that looks shareable and premium right out of the app.

Make a music player app for mobile where the cross-fade and gapless playback settings feel like a first-class feature rather than buried in some forgotten menu — the settings screen itself should look gorgeous, maybe with a soft waveform visual that shows how tracks blend into each other, and a smooth slider for adjusting the fade length so the transitions between songs feel exactly as seamless and atmospheric as you want them to be.

Need a music player app for my phone where the album art full-screen display is the real star of the experience — when a song plays the cover art should fill the entire screen with this lush, immersive presence, maybe with the background color shifting to match the artwork's palette, playback controls staying subtle and elegant so they don't break the mood, and the whole thing feeling like you're actually looking at the music rather than just hearing it.

Create a podcast player app for mobile that makes the transcript and chapter search feel beautifully integrated into the listening experience — instead of a wall of plain text, the transcript should flow with a gentle reading rhythm, highlighting the line being spoken in real time, and the chapter navigation should feel like flipping through a well-designed magazine so you can jump to exactly the conversation thread you came for without losing the atmosphere of the show.

Make a hashtag analytics tool for mobile that actually looks and feels as good as the content it's meant to support — a sleek, visually satisfying app where you can see which hashtags are performing, how reach trends over time, and what combinations drive the best engagement, with the data presented in a way that feels like a well-laid-out editorial spread rather than a dense spreadsheet, so it's genuinely enjoyable to open and review before you post.

Create a brand inspiration gallery app for mobile that collects real user-generated content in a way that feels curated rather than chaotic — the kind of tool a brand would actually want to use to gather and showcase community photos and posts, organized by theme or campaign with a warm, editorial grid layout that makes the content look elevated, so when you're scrolling through it on your phone it feels like a living mood board of what the brand actually means to real people.

Need a carousel content planner for my phone that helps me map out the visual flow of a multi-slide post before I hit publish — something with a light, editorial feel where each slide slot shows a small preview of the image or color and the caption idea, so I can see the whole sequence at a glance and rearrange until the story arc feels just right, with the overall layout giving off that calm, organized mood-board energy rather than a cluttered to-do list.

Need a mobile news reader app that just shows me a steady stream of articles I actually care about without making me dig around — I want to set a few topics I follow and have it pull in fresh stories every day, with each article showing the headline, a little summary, and where it's from so I can decide in one tap whether to read it or keep scrolling, all on my phone without fuss.

Create a simple news feed app for mobile that lets me scroll through the latest stories on topics I pick — something I can set up once with the subjects I care about and then just open it when I want to catch up, where the stories come in as clean little cards with a title and a short blurb, and I can tap to read the full thing or just keep going through the list without the app getting in my way.

A personal news feed app for my phone where you pick a handful of topics upfront and then the home screen just fills up with fresh articles about those things — each story shows up as a tidy little card with the headline and a two-sentence summary so you can decide instantly if it's worth your time, and there's a saved section where anything you tap to keep gets stored so you can actually go back and read it later.

Create a mobile reading app where corrections and update notices on articles are handled with real visual care — when a story has been corrected or updated, there should be a tasteful, clearly visible notice at the top of the article that feels honest and transparent without being jarring, showing what changed and when, styled in a way that respects both the reader's intelligence and the integrity of the piece, the kind of detail that makes the whole app feel trustworthy and well-edited.

Make a long-form article reader app for mobile where the source and citation reference list at the end of a piece is treated as something worth reading rather than an afterthought — the references should be laid out with a quiet, scholarly elegance, easy to scan and tap through, with each source showing the publication and author clearly so you feel like you're engaging with something genuinely researched and credible every time you reach the end of a well-reported story.

Create a news reading app for mobile where the paywall reminder and subscription prompt feels genuinely inviting rather than like a wall slamming down — when you hit the limit it should be a beautifully designed moment that shows you a glimpse of what you're missing, communicates the value clearly with a warm and confident tone, and makes the upgrade feel like joining something worth being part of, not like being punished for reading too much.

Build a subscription manager app for mobile that keeps all my news and content subscriptions in sync across devices — I want a clear list of everything I'm subscribed to, the ability to see what's active on each platform, and a simple way to make sure my reading preferences and followed topics carry over whether I'm on my phone or switching to another device, with a status indicator showing which sources are fully synced and which need attention.

Need a news source manager app for my phone that lets me filter sources by language and region — I follow news in a couple of different languages and from different parts of the world, so I want to be able to organize my sources by where they're from and what language they publish in, with a straightforward list I can check off to activate or pause sources by region, and a simple home screen that reflects exactly what I've set up.

A shared reading list app for mobile where you and a small group can all add articles and see what everyone else has saved — each person's additions show up labeled with their name, you can mark things as read or leave a short note about why you added something, and the whole list is kept tidy enough that catching up on what your group is reading feels easy and organized rather than like wading through a messy chat thread.

Need a news search app for my phone that has a dedicated toggle to show only exclusive investigations and deep-dive reporting — I'm tired of wading through wire reports and opinion pieces when I just want the original investigative stuff, so I want a search tool where I can flip that filter on and immediately narrow the results down to the real investigative journalism, with each result showing the outlet and publication date so I know what I'm getting.

Need a mobile app that lets me actually search through articles I've already saved or bookmarked — I have a huge backlog of saved stuff and right now finding anything in it is a nightmare, so I want a simple search bar inside my saved articles section where I can type a word or topic and it pulls up anything I've bookmarked that matches, sorted by when I saved it, so I can finally find that piece I set aside weeks ago without scrolling forever.

A topic alert tool built into the search flow of a mobile news app, where after you search for something you get a quick option to subscribe to alerts for that exact topic — so if I look up a court case or a company and want to stop manually checking back, I can just tap once right there in the search results to set up a notification that pings me whenever a new article about it comes in, with a simple list somewhere to manage and turn off the alerts I've set.

Create a product review app for mobile that lets me filter customer reviews by star rating so I can actually find the information I need — I want a clean, organized layout where I can tap a star tier to see just the five-star or just the two-star reviews, with each review showing the rating, the reviewer's name, the date, and the full comment, plus a summary at the top showing the breakdown across all ratings so I can make a quick decision before I buy.

Build a shopping cart app for mobile where every single item in my cart shows its own estimated delivery date right there in the list — I hate having to guess which things will arrive together or check each product page separately, so I want a cart summary where each item has a clear delivery estimate next to it, and if items are coming in separate shipments that's shown clearly too, so I know exactly what to expect before I hit checkout.

Build a package tracking app for mobile where I can easily reroute a delivery to a nearby parcel locker when I know I won't be home — I miss deliveries all the time and it's a hassle, so I want a tracker that shows my active orders and has a clear option on each one to redirect it to a locker location near me, with a simple map to pick the most convenient spot and a confirmation so I know the change went through before the driver shows up.
